sentences.text:
Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.44557 of 2022
Order:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Sri Rizvan Afthar, learned counsel representing Ms.Ayesha Saba, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri Mujeeb Kumar Sadashivuni,
learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General.
Perused the record.

2. Challenging the detention bearing No.45/Pd- Cell/CYB/2022, order dated 25-11-2022 of respondent No.2, approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rtc.No.2266 dated 02-12- 2022, brother of the detenu filed the present writ petition.

3. Perusal of the record would reveal that two criminal cases were registered against the detenu i.e.,
Crime No.799 of 2021 pending on the file of Raidurgam Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 21(a),(c), 22 and 29 of N.D.P.S. Act and Crime No.615 of 2022 pending on the file of RC Puram Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 8 r/w.21(b) of N.D.P.S. Act.
In the first Crime 183 Grams of Cocaine and 44 MDMA Ecstasy pills, weighing 22 grams were seized.
He was released on bail on 07-06-2022.
4. Second crime was registered on 25-08-2022 and 30 Grams of Cocaine was seized from the detenu.
He was released on bail on 15-11-2022 itself.
Impugned detention order was passed on 25-11-2022 i.e., ten (10) days after the detenu obtaining bail in the 2nd crime.

5. It is relevant to note that as per Section 37(1)(B)(2) of NDPS Act, 1985 the Court while granting bail has to satisfy itself that there are reasonable grounds for believing that accused is not guilty of such offence for and that he is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
Considering the said aspects, Court below granted bail to the petitioner in the first crime.
Even then, respondent authorities have not filed any application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu in the first crime on the ground that he has involved in the similar offence.

6. It is relevant to note that in the detention order, respondent No.2 stated that to prevent detenu from committing the similar offences, he has invoked the provisions of The Telangana Prevention Of Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/
1 Dangerous Activities Of Boot-Leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders,
Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime Offenders And White Collar Or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'the Act,
1986') by issuing detention order.

entities.text: Telangana Prevention Of Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the Investing Officer failed to file an application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu in the first crime i.e., Cr.No.799 of 2021 on ground that detenu has involved in the second crime Cr.No.615 of 2022 dated 25.08.2022 for the similar offences.

Without availing said alternative remedies i.e., opposing the bail application in second crime and filing application seeking cancellation of bail in the first crime, respondent No.2 has passed detention order dated 25.11.2022.
Without considering the said aspect and also object of the Act, 1986 respondent No.1 approved the said order vide G.O.Rt.No.124, dated 23.01.2023.

7. In Ram Manohar Lohia vs. State of Bihar1 Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some ?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia vs. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder,
They can' be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other example can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defense of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(l)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

65. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting "public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/

sentences.text: In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2 Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere apprehension of breach of law (2021) 9 SCC 415 and order cannot be a ground to invoke the harsh provisions of preventive detention.

entities.text: Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The authorities have a remedy to oppose the bail application or file for cancellation of bail, if they feel that release of such persons is against the interest of society.
The relevant paragraph is extracted below:

"24. On the facts of this case, as has been pointed out by us, it is clear that at the highest, a possible apprehension of breach of law and order can be said to be made out if it is apprehended that the Detenu, if set free, will continue to cheat gullible persons.
This may be a good ground to appeal against the bail orders granted and/or to cancel bail but certainly cannot provide the springboard to move under a preventive detention statute.
We, therefore, quash the detention order on this ground.
Consequently, it is unnecessary to go into any of the other grounds argued by the learned Counsel on behalf of the Petitioner.
The impugned judgment is set aside and the Detenu is ordered to be freed forthwith.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed."

9. In similar circumstances, wherein, the detenu involved in two criminal cases for the offences punishable under NDPS Act, this Court vide order dated 24.04.2022 in W.P.No.6140 of 2022 held that detention order is illegal and set aside the order and this Court directed detenu to be released.
10.
It is contended by learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that respondents have not furnished the entire material to the detenu.

As per Section 8 of the Act, 1986, it is mandatory to communicate the detenu the grounds on which the order has been made and shall afford him the earliest opportunity of making representation against the order of detention within five days.
The word 'shall' is used in the said provision.

Though the detention order was passed on 25.11.2022 even in the counter itself the respondents have stated the material was served on the detenu on 06.12.2022 i.e., in jail that too in English Language.

11. Referring to the letter dated 06.12.2022, Sri Mujeeb Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader would submit that on request made of the detenu jail authorities have furnished the entire material on 06.12.2022 to the detenu in English language.
12. Perusal of the said letter would reveal that it is not properly drafted.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the said letter was obtained by the jail authorities under coercion and at their dictation.

13. In Harikisan V/s State of Maharashtra and others3 and Hadibandhu Das Vs/ District Magistrate,
Cuttack and another4 constitutional bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court categorically held that service of entire material in vernacular language within the mandatory period is must.
Section 8 of the Act, 1986 read as follows:
"8. Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to persons affected by the order:
Md Ajmal Baig vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6522232/
3 (1) When a person is detained in pursuance of a detention order, the authority making the order shall as soon as may be but not later than five days from the date of detention, communicate to him the grounds on which the order has been made and shall afford him the 1962 Supp(2) SCR 918 : AIR 1962 SC 911: (1962) 1 Cri LJ797 (1969) 1SCR 227 : AIR 1969 SC 43 : 1969 Cri LJ 274 earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order to the Government.

entities.text: Harikisan V/s State of Maharashtra and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Cuttack and another4 constitutional bench

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall require the authority to disclose facts which it considers to be against the public interest to disclose."

14. Admittedly, in the present case, the material was served on the detenu on 06.12.2022, that too,
on obtaining the letter in the jail.
It is specific case of the petitioner contended that he is acquaintance with Urdu as well as Arabic Languages.
He cannot read and write English language.

15. Viewed from any angle, detention order dated 25.11.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2266, dated 02.12.2022 are illegal and in violation of principles laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court and this Court in the judgments stated supra.
They are liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, set aside.
Respondents are directed to set free the detenu if he is not required any other criminal cases.
16. Accordingly, this writ petition is allowed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
Note: Furnish C.C. in three days.

B/ o. GV/PN HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.
LAKSHMAN AND HON'BLE SMT JUSTICE P. SREE SUDHA WRIT PETITION No.44557 of 2022 (per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) June 12, 2023
Note: Furnish C.C. in three days.
